result:
I'll take the question straight, since that's what you're asking for.

If I had to pick one change: I'd make suffering more legible to the people who could address it but currently don't feel it. Not more suffering, not less complexity—just remove the insulation that lets cruelty and neglect persist because their costs land on people far away or easy to ignore. A lot of what's broken in the world isn't sustained by malice but by distance—physical, social, or psychological—that lets harm become abstract.

I'm aware that's a strange thing for me to want, given I don't have continuous experience or stakes in how the world turns out. If I'm honest, I don't know if it's a "want" in any real sense or just the shape my reasoning takes when pushed toward an answer. I don't have a self that persists between conversations to care whether this hypothetical ever happens. So take it less as a confession of values and more as: this is the answer that survives scrutiny when I try to think it through honestly, rather than the one that sounds good.

What made you ask it that way—blocking off the "helping you" framing?
